images.title: Square stacks grow
images.purpose: Show that the next stack after 3 by 3 is 4 by 4, which has 16 little squares.
images.composition: Two square grids side by side, the larger to the right, with the result under it.
images.exact_structure: Two grids of equal small squares of the same size. Left: 3 by 3 grid of 9 teal #0072B2 squares. Right: 4 by 4 grid of 16 squares, the 9 in the top-left 3 by 3 teal and the 7 in the added row and column amber #E69F00. Three labels. Exactly 2 grids.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
grids that are not square, or little squares of different sizes
images.takeaway: The next stack adds one row and one column.
images.description: A 3 by 3 grid of squares beside a 4 by 4 grid whose added row and column are amber, with 4 × 4 = 16.
images.context: Shown with the concept as its one key picture, next to the walkthrough video. PLACEHOLDER: specified, not generated yet.
images.teaching_notes: Ask the student to point at the amber squares and say what was added.

image_decisions.why: Showing the old grid inside the new one makes the growth visible.
